text: A list comprehension builds a whole list in one readable line, with no append loop required.
This one squares every number from zero to nine — the expression comes first, then the for.
Add an if on the end and it becomes a filter, so evens keeps only the multiples of two.
You can even nest two loops in a single comprehension, left to right, exactly like nested for statements.
This builds every x y pair where the two differ, skipping the diagonal.
Read it out loud and it says what it does — give me x times x, for x in range ten.
Now let's print all three and see exactly what we built.
Squares, evens and pairs — three data structures, three lines.
And not a single manual append anywhere.
Up next, decorators. Follow so you don't miss it.
